event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: LDOS’s 2023-02-14 filing shows that COVID-19 remains a live, material risk less than three years after the WHO declaration.  The company cites concrete, realized impacts—lower aviation-security sales, delayed contract awards, higher programme costs and continuing under-utilisation of its Security Enterprise Solutions unit—while also warning of potential long-term shifts in customer behaviour and revenues.  Although one sentence notes that fiscal-year-2022 results were not materially harmed and even records a $28 million recovery, that is framed as a partial offset to earlier stop-work disruptions.  Overall, the disclosures mix backward-looking evidence of actual financial and operational stress with forward-looking uncertainty, and they are sufficiently specific (naming business lines, contract delays and unrecoverable costs) to merit elevated—but not maximum—severity scores.  Applying the Time Decay Principle, the pandemic is a recent event (0-3 years), so scores in the 4-8 range are appropriate, with modest downward adjustments where the company highlights mitigating factors or lack of material 2022 impact.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which our business will be adversely affected by COVID-19 or other health epidemics, pandemics and similar outbreaks is highly uncertain and cannot be predicted.

components.reason: Acknowledges potential adverse effect from COVID-19 on the business.
Emphasises high uncertainty and lack of predictability, signalling ongoing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: States that COVID-19 could harm the business and the magnitude is unpredictable—clear but generic recent-event risk.

evidence_list.snippet: A disease pandemic, such as COVID-19 and its variants, or other widespread health epidemics, pandemics or similar outbreaks could create economic uncertainty and disruptions to the global economy that could adversely affect our businesses, or could lead to operational difficulties, including travel limitations, that could impair our ability to manage or conduct our business.

components.reason: Details economy-wide uncertainty and disruption that could adversely affect the company.
Specifies operational difficulties (travel limitations) that may impair business execution.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides specific operational channels (travel limits) through which the pandemic can hurt LDOS, yielding a moderate-high risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the global spread of COVID-19 resulted in a substantial decline in demand for air travel, which adversely impacted the demand for products and services related to our airport security detection and automation business.

components.reason: Describes an actual, realised impact (‘substantial decline’ in air-travel demand).
Links directly to a specific revenue stream (airport security detection and automation).
Uses strong wording (‘substantial’) underscoring severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete evidence of pandemic-driven revenue reduction in a named business line; high severity but unquantified, so 7/10.

evidence_list.snippet: We are not able to predict whether COVID-19 will result in permanent changes to air travel behaviors, including a permanent reduction in business travel as a result of the increased use of teleconferencing products and, more broadly, a general reluctance by consumers to travel, each of which has, and could continue to, impact our business.

components.reason: Raises possibility of permanent behavioural shifts reducing future demand.
Acknowledges both past and continuing impact on business.
Expresses uncertainty about magnitude/duration, signalling ongoing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking risk of lasting demand change coupled with acknowledgement of current impact warrants above-average score.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, new contract awards have been and may continue to be delayed and our ability to perform on our existing contracts has been and may continue to be delayed or impaired, which will negatively impact our revenues.

components.reason: Reports pandemic-driven delays in new contract awards (historical and prospective).
Notes impairment to performance on existing contracts.
Explicitly links to negative revenue impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies concrete revenue risk through both award and execution delays—high severity though not quantified.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, our program costs have increased as a result of COVID-19, and these cost increases may not be fully recoverable or adequately covered by insurance or equitable adjustments to contract prices.

components.reason: States direct cost increases attributable to COVID-19.
Warns that increased costs may not be recoverable, elevating financial risk.
Highlights lack of mitigation (insurance or contract adjustments may be inadequate).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete cost inflation with limited recovery options reflects significant financial exposure.

evidence_list.snippet: For fiscal 2022, the COVID-19 pandemic did not have a material impact to revenues and operating income, other than the receipt of $28 million in recoveries, within our Health segment related to stop work orders on certain programs.

components.reason: States that 2022 revenue impact was not material (mitigating).
Quantifies $28 million recovery, indicating a positive offset.
Nevertheless references prior stop-work orders caused by COVID-19 (evidence of disruption).
Provides specific dollar figure, adding transparency to risk history.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Although it quantifies a recovery and minimises 2022 impact, the snippet still evidences prior COVID-linked disruptions, yielding a low residual score.

evidence_list.snippet: The volume of global passenger air travel remains below pre-pandemic levels, which continues to impact the operations of our Security Enterprise Solutions reporting unit.

components.reason: Indicates ongoing industry metric (air travel) has not rebounded.
Connects that shortfall directly to operational impact on a named business unit.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows a continuing, business-line-specific operational drag tied to the pandemic; solid but unquantified impact.

evidence_list.snippet: The full extent of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on our operational and financial performance, including our ability to execute on programs in the expected timeframe, will depend on future developments, including the duration and spread of the pandemic and the distribution of vaccines, all of which are uncertain and cannot be predicted.

components.reason: States that operational and financial impacts hinge on uncertain future developments.
Highlights risk to program execution timelines.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic but timely statement of uncertainty and potential execution risk—moderate severity.
